ayahLayers.grammar: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ is a relative clause identifying the people mentioned in the preceding verse. هُمْ begins a nominal sentence; عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ is a prepositional phrase linked to سَاهُونَ, which is its predicate.
ayahLayers.contextualMeaning: Those who are heedless and neglectful regarding their prayer.
sentenceMap: ٱلَّذِينَ — relative pronoun introducing the description
هُمْ — detached pronoun, the topic of the nominal clause
عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ — prepositional phrase, away from/regarding their prayer

teaching.rootPicture: Rootless fixed grammatical form: memorize ٱلَّذِينَ as the masculine-plural form meaning those who.
teaching.construction: A fixed masculine-plural relative pronoun that introduces a describing clause.
teaching.grammar: It introduces the relative clause and identifies the people described as heedless of prayer; it connects back to the preceding mention of those who pray.
teaching.sentenceRole: Relative-clause introducer and modifier of the preceding noun phrase.
teaching.recognitionClue: The ending ـذِينَ is a strong clue for the masculine-plural relative pronoun ٱلَّذِينَ.
teaching.takeaway: Recognize ٱلَّذِينَ as the gateway to a description of a group: those who ...

layers.occurrenceRole: Introduces the relative description of the people addressed in the preceding verse.

morphology.notes: The plural form is used for a masculine or mixed-gender group.

layers.grammar: Masculine-plural relative pronoun introducing a relative clause.
learnerConnections: Connect ٱلَّذِينَ with the singular relative pronoun ٱلَّذِي: the ending marks a plural group.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: Spot ٱلَّذِينَ before a clause that explains which people are meant.
pedagogy.explanation: It is not a derived noun with a root here; it is a fixed connector that opens the description.
pedagogy.takeaway: Read ٱلَّذِينَ as those who and expect the following words to describe them.

teaching.rootPicture: Rootless grammatical form: هُمْ is a fixed pronoun for a masculine or mixed group.
teaching.construction: A standalone third-person masculine-plural pronoun used here before its predicate.
teaching.grammar: It is the topic/subject of the nominal sentence هُمْ ... سَاهُونَ.
teaching.sentenceRole: Topic of the nominal clause whose predicate is سَاهُونَ.
teaching.recognitionClue: The final مْ identifies the familiar detached pronoun هُمْ: they.
teaching.takeaway: هُمْ can stand alone as they and can set up a nominal sentence.

layers.occurrenceRole: Topic of the nominal sentence describing the group.

morphology.notes: The same form can refer to a masculine or mixed-gender plural group.

layers.grammar: Detached third-person masculine-plural pronoun functioning as the topic of the nominal clause.
learnerConnections: Compare هُمْ with the suffix ـهِمْ in صَلَاتِهِمْ: both point to the same they/their group.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: When هُمْ appears independently, first test the meaning they before treating it as a verb ending.
pedagogy.explanation: Arabic can place a detached pronoun before a verbal sentence or predicate to make the subject explicit.
pedagogy.takeaway: Separate هُمْ as the pronoun they; do not attach it to the neighboring word.

teaching.rootPicture: Rootless function word: عَن signals relation or distance rather than naming an action.
teaching.construction: A standalone preposition governing the following noun phrase صَلَاتِهِمْ.
teaching.grammar: It places صَلَاتِهِمْ in the genitive and forms the phrase عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ.
teaching.sentenceRole: Introduces the prepositional phrase linked to the predicate سَاهُونَ.
teaching.recognitionClue: عَن before a noun often gives a meaning such as from, about, or away from.
teaching.takeaway: Read عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ as a unit: regarding or away from their prayer.

layers.occurrenceRole: Preposition introducing the object of heedlessness: their prayer.

morphology.notes: Its contextual force here is distance or neglect in relation to prayer.

layers.grammar: Preposition governing صَلَاتِهِمْ and connecting the phrase to سَاهُونَ.
learnerConnections: Learn عَن as a relation word whose exact English rendering depends on the surrounding verb or adjective.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: A short standalone word before a noun is often a preposition; عَن commonly carries from/about/away from meanings.
pedagogy.explanation: Here the phrase is not simply about the prayer as a topic; it describes heedlessness in relation to it.
pedagogy.takeaway: Keep عَن attached in meaning to the phrase that follows it.

teaching.rootPicture: ص ل و is associated with prayer and connection in ṣalāh; picture an act of prayer connecting the worshipper to Allah.
teaching.construction: صَلَاة with the attached third-person plural possessive suffix ـهِمْ; the noun is in the construct relationship and appears genitive after عَن.
teaching.grammar: The phrase is governed by عَن. صَلَاتِ is the noun, and ـهِمْ means their; the kasra before the suffix reflects the phrase's genitive position.
teaching.sentenceRole: Object of the preposition عَن within the predicate phrase عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ.
teaching.recognitionClue: The ending ـهِمْ is the attached their/them suffix; the noun before it carries the possessed item.
teaching.takeaway: صَلَاتِهِمْ = صَلَاة + هِمْ: their prayer; the suffix turns prayer into a possessed noun.

layers.occurrenceRole: Genitive object of عَن and the prayer that the group is heedless regarding.

morphology.notes: The final ة of the citation form appears as ت when the possessive suffix is attached: صَلَاتِهِمْ.

layers.grammar: A noun plus attached third-person masculine-plural possessive pronoun, governed by عَن in a genitive prepositional phrase.
learnerConnections: Compare ـهِمْ here with standalone هُمْ in the same ayah: the suffix means their, while the independent form means they.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: When ـهِمْ is attached to a noun, translate it as their and look left for what they possess.
pedagogy.explanation: The surface form صَلَاتِهِمْ is complete: prayer plus their. The ت is the visible form of the feminine ending before the suffix.
pedagogy.takeaway: Read the phrase as one meaning unit: their prayer, while still noticing the possessive suffix.

teaching.rootPicture: س ه و evokes drifting into forgetfulness or inattention; picture the mind wandering away from what it should attend to.
teaching.construction: Active participle سَاهٍ from the root س-ه-و, here in the sound masculine plural form سَاهُونَ.
teaching.grammar: It is the nominative predicate of هُمْ. The ending ـونَ marks masculine plural in the nominative.
teaching.sentenceRole: Predicate describing the group's heedlessness regarding prayer.
teaching.recognitionClue: The ending ـونَ commonly signals a sound masculine plural in the nominative; the stem سَاهُ carries the lexical meaning.
teaching.takeaway: سَاهُونَ describes an ongoing quality: being heedless or inattentive toward prayer.

layers.occurrenceRole: Predicate of هُمْ, completing the description of the people as heedless.

morphology.notes: The singular citation form is سَاهٍ; this occurrence is the nominative plural سَاهُونَ.

layers.grammar: Nominative predicate of the nominal sentence هُمْ سَاهُونَ.
learnerConnections: Recognize ـونَ as a nominative masculine-plural ending and compare it with the accusative/genitive ـينَ pattern.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: See ـونَ at the end and test a sound masculine plural; then read سَاهُ as the stem meaning heedless.
pedagogy.explanation: The word describes a settled quality or behavior, not just a one-time act of forgetting.
pedagogy.takeaway: The clause says they are characterized by heedlessness toward prayer.

ayahLayers.grammar: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَآءُونَ adds a second relative description. ٱلَّذِينَ introduces the clause, هُمْ makes the group explicit, and يُرَآءُونَ is the plural imperfect verb describing their act of showing off.
ayahLayers.contextualMeaning: Those who show off, performing religious acts for the sight or praise of others.
sentenceMap: ٱلَّذِينَ — relative pronoun introducing the second description
هُمْ — detached pronoun making the subject explicit
يُرَآءُونَ — third-person masculine-plural imperfect verb: they show off

teaching.rootPicture: Rootless fixed grammatical form: memorize ٱلَّذِينَ as the masculine-plural form meaning those who.
teaching.construction: A fixed masculine-plural relative pronoun that introduces another description of the same group.
teaching.grammar: It opens the relative clause whose predicate is the verbal sentence هُمْ يُرَآءُونَ.
teaching.sentenceRole: Relative-clause introducer for the description of those who show off.
teaching.recognitionClue: The ending ـذِينَ is a strong clue for the masculine-plural relative pronoun ٱلَّذِينَ.
teaching.takeaway: The repeated ٱلَّذِينَ signals another identifying description of the people.

layers.occurrenceRole: Introduces a second relative description parallel to the description in ayah 5.

morphology.notes: Its repeated occurrence preserves the parallel structure of the two descriptions.

layers.grammar: Masculine-plural relative pronoun introducing a relative clause.
learnerConnections: Compare this occurrence with ٱلَّذِينَ in 107:5: the form is unchanged, while the following clause supplies a new description.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: Repeated ٱلَّذِينَ means the reader should look for another clause describing the same kind of group.
pedagogy.explanation: Arabic repeats the relative pronoun here to add a parallel characterization: those who show off.
pedagogy.takeaway: Use the repeated connector to see the parallel relationship between ayahs 5 and 6.

teaching.rootPicture: Rootless grammatical form: هُمْ is a fixed pronoun for a masculine or mixed group.
teaching.construction: A standalone third-person masculine-plural pronoun placed before the verbal predicate يُرَآءُونَ.
teaching.grammar: It makes the subject explicit; the following plural verb agrees with the same group.
teaching.sentenceRole: Explicit subject/topic of the verbal sentence describing their showing off.
teaching.recognitionClue: The final مْ identifies the detached pronoun هُمْ: they.
teaching.takeaway: Here هُمْ points forward to the people who perform the action in يُرَآءُونَ.

layers.occurrenceRole: Explicit subject of the clause whose verb is يُرَآءُونَ.

morphology.notes: The pronoun is repeated to make the subject of the second description explicit.

layers.grammar: Detached third-person masculine-plural pronoun functioning as the explicit subject/topic before the verbal predicate.
learnerConnections: Compare the same هُمْ in 107:5: the form stays the same while the following predicate changes from سَاهُونَ to يُرَآءُونَ.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: When هُمْ appears before a plural verb, use it as the explicit they and confirm agreement in the verb.
pedagogy.explanation: The detached pronoun and the plural verb together make the actors unmistakable.
pedagogy.takeaway: Read هُمْ ... يُرَآءُونَ as they show off.

parts.label: imperfect verb stem with third-person prefix
parts.meaning: show off; seek to be seen

teaching.meaning: they show off; they seek to be seen
teaching.rootPicture: ر أ ي is connected with seeing; رَاءَى turns that idea into acting so that others see the act.
teaching.construction: Form III verb رَاءَى, with the imperfect prefix يُـ and the third-person masculine-plural ending ـونَ: يُرَآءُونَ.
teaching.grammar: Third-person masculine-plural imperfect indicative. The wāw in ـونَ is the plural subject marker and the nūn is retained in the indicative.
teaching.sentenceRole: Verbal predicate describing the action performed by هُمْ.
teaching.recognitionClue: The prefix يُـ marks a third-person masculine imperfect verb; ـونَ marks they in the plural indicative.

forms.meaning: to engage in or deliberately perform an action toward another
forms.difference: Here رَاءَى means to act for display, seeking to be seen or praised by people.

teaching.takeaway: يُرَآءُونَ describes deliberate public display: they show off rather than act solely for Allah.

layers.occurrenceRole: Plural imperfect predicate describing the group's ostentatious action.

morphology.notes: The wāw of ـونَ marks the plural subject; the nūn is the indicative ending.

layers.grammar: Third-person masculine-plural imperfect indicative verb functioning as the predicate of هُمْ.
layers.meaning: they show off; they seek to be seen
learnerConnections: Connect the root ر-أ-ي with seeing and notice how Form III gives the idea of making an action visible to others.

pedagogy.recognitionClue: ُيـ at the beginning plus ـونَ at the end is a useful frame for a third-person masculine-plural imperfect verb.
pedagogy.explanation: The meaning is more than simply doing: the verb expresses displaying an act so that people notice it.
pedagogy.takeaway: Hear the contrast between sincere worship and يُرَآءُونَ, acting for public appearance.
